day_shape: 53 items: Araghchi-Lammy phone call confirmed by Tehran, UK charges dual national over IRGC surveillance of RAF Cyprus base, Board of Peace publishes Gaza disarmament roadmap with two-week ceasefire, White House renews Lebanon national emergency, Defa Press claims Strait of Hormuz transit suspended, heavy Arbaeen coverage on IRIB.

threads.label: Gaza ceasefire and disarmament roadmap
threads.summary: The Board of Peace released the full text of a roadmap implementing Trump's Gaza plan, with a two-week ceasefire to finalise Hamas disarmament and no IDF withdrawal from the Yellow Line until complete. A Hamas official said the group would refuse to implement the deal without Israeli endorsement; US and BoP officials called it a 'breakthrough'.

threads.label: IDF strikes on Hamas operatives in Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing in a Thursday Gaza City strike of Abd al-Rahim Kardi, a deputy Hamas cell commander who held hostages Romi Gonen and Noa Marciano. Separate strikes killed Hamas supply officer Muhammad al-Abed, commander Ahmad Anqar, and Mujahideen Brigades commander Ahmed Kafina, involved in the October 7 abductions of Avinatan Or and Noa Argamani.

threads.label: UK-Iran diplomatic and espionage strands
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB reported a Friday phone call between Foreign Minister Araghchi and UK Foreign Secretary David Lammy on bilateral and regional matters. Separately, a dual British-Azerbaijani national was arrested in Cyprus and charged in the first overseas case under Britain's National Security Act with surveilling an RAF base for the IRGC.

threads.label: Regime war narrative and Hormuz claim
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB posted a Strait of Hormuz Waterway Management Authority notice claiming transit is not possible due to US military actions, alongside IRIB items citing WSJ on Iranian missile and drone strikes on Kuwaiti infrastructure and claiming US expenditure of 1,500 Patriot and 200 THAAD interceptors. Khamenei's office published a message stating studies have been conducted on opening new fronts where the enemy is 'severely vulnerable'.

threads.label: Iran illicit finance and cyber allegations
threads.summary: A Reuters investigation cited by Iran International found an Iranian gambling network moved at least $4 billion through an unlicensed Dubai crypto exchange also handling sanctioned Iranian institutions' funds. The Jerusalem Post reported US officials suspect Iran of a cyberattack targeting over 30 municipal water systems in Minnesota.

events.title_en: Special stamp for the Arbaeen walk of Imam Hussein unveiled
events.summary_en: Special stamp for the Arbaeen walk of Imam Hussein unveiled. The unveiling ceremony for the special Arbaeen stamp of the year 1405 AH - 1448 AH was held with the presence of Seyyed Sattar Hashemi, Minister of Communications and Information Technology, a number of officials from Iranian and Iraqi postal services and officials from the Consulate General of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Karbala. The special Arbaeen stamp was designed and published with the aim of honouring the world's largest gathering of faith and celebrating Ashura culture. In the design of this stamp, the millions-strong pilgrimage of the devotees of Imam Hussein (peace be upon him) is depicted and the phrase 'Love of Hussein unites us' serves as a symbol of Muslim unity, harmony and solidarity.

events.summary_en: The Guardian: Strange US mistake; names of all African countries jumbled on map. The US State Department at a global AIDS conference in Brazil displayed a map of Africa in which the names of all countries were incorrectly placed. On this map, Nigeria was moved to the Sahara and shown as a landlocked country; Mozambique and Ivory Coast were also thousands of kilometres away from their actual positions. Investigations show this map was created using artificial intelligence tools from the company OpenAI. events.summary_en: Depleted US missile reserves. The US International and Strategic Studies Centre has announced that the United States has expended 1,500 Patriot missiles and 200 THAAD interceptors in its confrontation with Iran. German sources have also reported that Patriot missile interceptor stocks have been depleted in Ukraine. Previously, most of the other European countries' Patriot missiles were transferred to western Asia for use in the war against Iran.

events.title: Two Hamas operatives who were advancing attacks on troops were killed in strikes in the Gaza Strip on Wednesday, the military says. The IDF says the strikes killed Muhammad al-Abed, a supply officer, and Ahmad Ma'in Muhammad Anqar, a commander in the terror group. Abed had been involved in "smuggling weapons into the Gaza Strip and digging smuggling tunnels while supplying weapons to the military wings," during the war, according to the IDF. The IDF justifies the strike amid the ceasefire by saying that recently, both operatives had been advancing attacks. "The terrorists posed a threat to IDF troops and were eliminated in precise aerial strikes," the military adds.

events.title: Tehran prosecutor takes legal action against opponents of executions
events.summary: Tehran's prosecutor has launched legal action against an unspecified number of people for opposing the execution of detainees arrested during the January protests and defendants convicted in cases linked to the recent war, Iran's judiciary news outlet Mizan reported on Thursday.
